# Transition-state symmetry and molecular graph representations

This task uses ordinary transition-state theory (TST) and the graph
representation conventions of the Auto-Mech project.  The following context is
provided as a method reference, not as a solution for this particular source
snapshot.

For a reaction rate in canonical TST, a common schematic form is

\[
k(T) = \frac{k_B T}{h}\frac{Q^\ddagger(T)}{Q_R(T)}
       \exp\left[-\frac{\Delta E^\ddagger}{k_B T}\right],
\]

where the molecular partition functions contain translational, rotational, and
vibrational contributions. The rotational contribution for a nonlinear
molecule contains a symmetry divisor \(\sigma\):

\[
q_{\mathrm{rot}} \propto \frac{1}{\sigma}
  \sqrt{I_A I_B I_C}\,T^{3/2},
\]

with the corresponding expression for a linear molecule using its nonzero
moments of inertia. The symmetry number is a property of the physical
molecular object and its indistinguishable rotations; equivalent presentations
of one object must not change the physical factor. See Truhlar, Garrett, and
Klippenstein, *Current Status of Transition-State Theory*,
<https://doi.org/10.1021/cr00016a001>.
